introduction-the-silent-failure.core: Bad data rarely crashes pipelines. It silently flows downstream, corrupting dashboards and models. Data quality engineering adds contracts (agreed schemas and semantics), tests (expectations) and drift monitoring to catch problems at the source.

first_principles.problem: An upstream team renames a field, nulls flood a column, and a pricing model quietly makes bad predictions for two weeks.
truths: Data producers and consumers are often different teams.
Silent errors are the most expensive.

analogy.title: A water treatment plant downstream of a leak
analogy.story: If sewage leaks upstream, the downstream plant can't tell until people get sick, unless there are sensors.
analogy.breaks: You can't test every property, so focus on what consumers depend on.

example.title: A silent failure
flow: Upstream changes currency from USD to cents

steps.label: Lesson
steps.detail: A green pipeline doesn't mean correct data.

check.q: Why are data quality failures especially dangerous?
check.a: They usually don't crash pipelines, so bad data flows silently into dashboards and models.

data-contracts-schema-registries.core: A data contract is an API-like agreement between producer and consumers: schema, types, semantics, constraints, freshness SLAs and evolution rules. Schema registries (Confluent, Apicurio) enforce compatible evolution for streaming data and reject breaking changes at publish time.

first_principles.problem: Producers change event formats without warning, breaking every downstream consumer.
truths: Data is an interface between teams.
derivation: **Define the contract**: schema (Avro/Protobuf/JSON Schema), owners, SLAs.

analogy.title: An API contract for data
analogy.story: Just as an API promises its request and response shape, a data contract promises the shape and meaning of the data.
analogy.breaks: Schemas don't capture all semantics (units, meanings), so document those in the contract too.

example.title: Backward compatibility rejection
flow: Producer tries to remove required field 'amount'
Producer adds new optional field instead

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Breaking changes are stopped at the source.

example.outcome: data interfaces as stable as APIs.

check.q: What does a schema registry's compatibility check prevent?
check.a: Producers publishing schema changes that would break existing consumers.

data-as-code-great-expectations-soda.core: Write unit tests for data: expectations such as 'not null', 'unique', 'between 0 and 1', 'row count within ±10% of yesterday' or 'values in this set'. Tools like Great Expectations, Soda and dbt tests run them in pipelines and block bad data before it propagates.

first_principles.problem: Schema checks pass, but the data is wrong: nulls, duplicates, impossible values, missing partitions.

analogy.title: Quality control on a production line
analogy.story: Inspect each batch before it ships; reject defective batches.
analogy.breaks: Too many brittle tests cause alert fatigue, so test what matters.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Bad batches never reach dashboards or models.

code.text:
checks for orders:
  - row_count > 1000
  - missing_count(customer_id) = 0
  - duplicate_count(order_id) = 0
  - invalid_percent(status) = 0:
      valid values: [paid, refunded, pending]
  - freshness(created_at) < 2h

check.q: Give two examples of data quality expectations.
check.a: For example, a column has no nulls, and values fall within an allowed range (also uniqueness, freshness and volume checks).

the-silent-killers-data-drift-vs-concept.core: Data drift: input distributions shift (users get younger, a new region is added). Concept drift: the relationship between inputs and outcomes changes (fraud patterns evolve). Both degrade models without any schema change, so monitor distributions and performance and retrain as needed.

first_principles.problem: A model's accuracy slowly decays over months while every data check passes.
truths: Models learn a snapshot of relationships.
derivation: **Data drift**: compare feature distributions (PSI, KS test) against training.
**Concept drift**: track live performance when labels arrive.

analogy.title: A weather forecaster's rules going stale
analogy.story: Rules learned from past climate fail as the climate changes (concept), or the forecaster moves to a new city (data).
analogy.breaks: Labels often arrive late, so concept drift detection lags and proxies help.

example.title: Detecting drift

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Degradation is caught before business impact.

example.outcome: models that stay accurate as the world changes.

check.q: What's the difference between data drift and concept drift?
check.a: Data drift is a change in input distributions; concept drift is a change in the relationship between inputs and the target.
